# Introduction

Kernel density estimation is a non-parametric way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable [@Rice2007, p390].
The kernel density estimate (KDE) is defined as:
$$
  \hat{f}(x) = \frac{1}{nh} \sum_{i = 1}^n K\left(\frac{x - x_i}{h}\right),
$$ {#eq-kde}
where $K$ is the kernel function, $h$ is the bandwidth, and $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ are the observed data points.
A common kernel function is the Gaussian kernel, defined as:
$$
  K(u) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-u^2/2}.
$$

@fig-density shows a KDE computed using @eq-kde with a Gaussian kernel, and $h$ chosen using the Sheather-Jones method [@SJ91].

```{r}
#| label: fig-density
#| fig-cap: A kernel density estimate obtained using 200 simulated data points from a N(0,1) distribution.
#| echo: true

library(tidyverse)
set.seed(2022 - 12 - 20)
df <- tibble(x = rnorm(200))
df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_density(bw = "sj") +
  geom_rug()
```
